packages.label: מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וּקְלִפּוֹת
packages.reason: The Rebbe explicitly equates three concepts using 'הוּא' (IS) language — the language of bechina: (1) every מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה (foreign thought) IS a קְלִפָּה (spiritual husk), and (2) the קְלִפָּה IS a קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה (complete spiritual stature/form). These three are explicitly stated to be the same thing. All belong to the evil domain: they are the opposing forces that invade the space of prayer and must be defeated. The foreign thought, the husk, and the complete-form are three faces of the same spiritual opponent.

packages.label: תְּפִלָּה כְּסֵדֶר וְגִבּוּרַת הַהִלּוּךְ
packages.label_en: Ordered Prayer and the Strength of Forward Movement
packages.reason: The Rebbe presents a set of concepts that all share the same essential nature — the positive force that defeats the foreign thoughts: תְּפִלָּה כְּסֵדֶר (prayer in order) IS the warrior's march (דֶּרֶךְ הִלּוּכוֹ), and this movement IS itself the defeat. The גִּבּוּר (warrior/brave person) who passes through the ambushers without looking back (אֵינוֹ מַשְׁגִּיחַ / לִבְלִי לְהִסְתַּכֵּל) is the same essential figure as the person praying in order. The not-looking (אֵינוֹ מַשְׁגִּיחַ) is the bechina of the forward movement — they are two expressions of the same stance of non-engagement. Together these concepts define the domain of victorious prayer as a single unbroken forward movement.
